# Kostiantyn Denysov

> Technical Lead at Deel in Berlin, leading release engineering and developer experience for a globally distributed engineering organization. About ten years in backend and platform engineering, from fullstack engineer to backend technical lead, staff engineer and now release engineering lead.

## Blog
- [All posts](https://denysov.me/blog/): Short, practical posts on release engineering, developer experience, engineering leadership and building with AI. By Kostiantyn Denysov, Berlin.
- [Who learns to code when AI writes the code?](https://denysov.me/blog/who-learns-to-code-when-ai-writes-the-code/) (2026-11-24): AI writes the easy code that junior developers used to learn on. What teams lose when nobody struggles with the basics, and what tech leads can do.
- [HIT-6, MIDAS and MSQ-21 in plain words](https://denysov.me/blog/hit-6-midas-and-msq-21-in-plain-words/) (2026-11-17): Your neurologist may hand you three short questionnaires. Here is what HIT-6, MIDAS and MSQ measure, how they are scored, and why a diary helps.
- [Boring deploys are the goal](https://denysov.me/blog/boring-deploys-are-the-goal/) (2026-11-10): A good release is a non-event. Here is how small batches, automation and fast rollback make deploys boring, and what that looks like on a dashboard.
- [How I build side projects with AI: 7 rules that work](https://denysov.me/blog/building-a-side-project-with-ai/) (2026-11-08): How I build real side projects with AI coding tools, and what I recommend. Keep the scope small, write the spec first, test everything, and stay the engineer.

## Focus
Release management, CI/CD, database migrations, internal developer tooling, blameless incident reviews, system design, mentoring. TypeScript, Node.js, Go, C#/.NET, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, Pulumi, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kafka, PostgreSQL, MongoDB.

- [Parley](https://parley.trading): open-source terminal app where six AI investor personas debate a stock
